messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: SEV2 - EU region error rate spike: 5xx up 12% over 5m, request failures concentrated on /v1/generate. Suspected recent rollout: rollout-id=rl-2026-03-17-eu-12.
maria (oncall): acked, I'm on it. pulling recent deploys and flags now.
ajay: checking model-serving metrics — canary showed higher latency earlier but 5xxs look new. did we flip any routing flags this morning?
devon (deploy-bot): recent ops: rollout rl-2026-03-17-eu-12 (weight 30% -> 70% green) at 3461238400. feature flag set: new-egress-path=true (config cfg-911).
leo: under load the green pool is returning upstream 502s from edge-proxy; blue pool looks fine. logs show backend 502 from eu-green-0 and eu-green-1.
maria (oncall): can we kill the flag or abort the rollout? priority: get responses back to normal for customers.
devon (deploy-bot): you can abort rollout:
```
redwoodctl rollout abort rl-2026-03-17-eu-12 --confirm
```
will start immediate traffic reweight to blue.
maria (oncall): doing abort now.
(maria (oncall) invoked command)
devon (deploy-bot): rollout abort accepted. initiating rollback and reweight -> blue=100%, estimated shift 30s.
incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: rollback in progress — traffic shifting from green to blue.
natalie: support seeing dozens of customer tickets: intermittent 502/504, some timeouts from EU tenants. can ops confirm if we need to open SEV3 customer comms?
ajay: capture quick healthcheck result from both pools:
```
# curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://eu-green-0.internal/v1/health
502 0.42
# curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://eu-blue-0.internal/v1/health
200 0.05
```
leo: logs (last 10 lines) show upstream proxy returning 502 with body "upstream read timeout" for green instances:```
[2026-03-17T09:12:01Z] eu-green-0 upstream read timeout
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] eu-green-1 upstream read timeout
```
maria (oncall): looks like green pool is unhealthy. rollback is correct. however some clients are still hitting stale DNS/cache entries and seeing errors. what's our TTL?
devon (deploy-bot): edge DNS TTL is 300s, but we also have sticky session cookies and CDN edges with longer TTL. we are forcing immediate reweight at LB as workaround.
leo: executing weight flip at ALB now (manual step from runbook 7.2):
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:... --default-actions 'Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=eu-blue-tg,Order=1'
```
leo: change applied. traffic should be cut over even if DNS cache persists.
incident-bot: ROLLBACK COMPLETE: blue=100% at 3461239980. 5xx rate trending down.
natalie: customer impact summary for on-call handoff: ~87 failed requests across 12 tenants in last 15m, peak 09:12Z. no major revenue-impacting customers on pager but a few enterprise customers reported degraded UX. drafting comms.
maria (oncall): good work. starting short postmortem notes: cause suspected: new-egress-path introduced an edge-proxy incompatibility under specific header patterns -> caused upstream read timeouts on green.
ajay: collecting traces and request ids for 5xxs, will attach to postmortem. also validate whether the flag gating logic missed a fallback.
sara: i'm taking over monitoring and next-oncall handoff in 35m. maria — please include me on the incident channel and leave runbook pointers.
maria (oncall): handing off now. summary: SEV2 -> rolled back rl-2026-03-17-eu-12, aborted flag new-egress-path, forced LB weight to blue, DNS TTL means some clients still erroring until caches expire. support to send initial status to affected customers. attach logs/traces link: https://internal.redwood/incident/3461239876.
sara: got it, taking over monitoring and the postmortem. will coordinate follow-up with runtime and deploy teams. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: NOTE: next steps — collect flag evaluation events, kernel/edge-proxy metrics, and canary telemetry. schedule postmortem within 48h.
natalie: support will send a targeted note to the 12 affected tenants with remediation steps and apology. will include timeline and workaround (no action required, auto-recovery after cache expiry or reload).
maria (oncall): closing active mitigation. remaining tasks assigned to sara and ajay for 4h. handing off full context.
sara: acknowledged. monitoring until stabilised. if error rate rises back above 3% alert me immediately.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) at 3461240200 - customer impact reduced, blue stable. postmortem pending.
